subject: sociology
title: Labels in Schools and Streets
welcome_lead: From classroom 'troublemakers' to media 'folk devils', see labels in action in real studies.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure applying labelling theory to school, crime, mods and rockers.
final_note: Always pair a label with a study and an outcome — that nails AO2.

concepts.def: Person lives up or down to a label.
Label that overrides all other identities.
Reactions to a label make deviance worse.
Cohen: groups blamed in moral panics.
Exaggerated public fear of a group.

walkthroughs.body_html: Rosenthal and Jacobson (1968) told teachers some pupils were 'gifted' (when they were random). Months later those pupils improved more — proof of self-fulfilling prophecy.
Becker showed how labels become a master status. A teenager labelled 'criminal' may struggle to get jobs, mix with other labelled peers and drift into a deviant career — deviance amplification.
Stan Cohen's 1972 study of mods and rockers showed how media exaggerate a small clash into a moral panic. The group becomes a folk devil, more young people copy, and the cycle grows.
